results.question: selection sort คือ
results.first_source:
Selection sort divides the array into a finalized sorted prefix and an unresolved suffix. On pass i,
inspect every record in the suffix and remember the position of a smallest key. Exchange that
record with A[i]. Continue until only one unresolved record remains.
The scan determines where the minimum is; it does not need to rearrange the array while
searching. This is the essential distinction from bubble sort, which performs local exchanges
during its scan. Both can move a minimum to the left boundary, but selection uses one direct
exchange rather than a chain of adjacent exchanges.

results.question: insertion sort คือ
results.first_source:
We start with insertion sort, which is an efﬁcient algorithm for sorting a small
number of elements. Insertion sort works the way many people sort a hand of
playing cards. We start with an empty left hand and the cards face down on the
table. We then remove one card at a time from the table and insert it into the
correct position in the left hand. To ﬁnd the correct position for a card, we compare
it with each of the cards already in the hand, from right to left, as illustrated in
Figure 2.1. At all times, the cards held in the left hand are sorted, and these cards
were originally the top cards of the pile on the table.

results.question: counting sort คือ
results.first_source:
8.2
Counting sort
Counting sort assumes that each of the n input elements is an integer in the range
0 to k, for some integer k. When k = O(n), the sort runs in Θ(n) time.
